data.theorem_title: $f(1)/f(n)=n^s$: the top item is $n^s$ times as frequent as the $n$-th
data.formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipfPMF_ratio (N : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hn1 : 1 ≤ n) (hnN : n ≤ N) :
    zipfPMF N s 1 / zipfPMF N s n = (n : ℝ) ^ s := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
data.natural_language_statement:
For $1\le n\le N$ and real $s$, the most probable item is exactly $n^s$ times as probable as the item of rank $n$:
$$\frac{f(1;N,s)}{f(n;N,s)}=n^{s}.$$
For $s=1$: the most common word occurs $n$ times as often as the $n$-th most common one.
data.source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law), snapshot uploaded by the proposer, lead section and "Word frequencies in human languages" ("the most common word occurs about n times the n-th most common one").
